theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a compliance audit?
options: To set the sales and service targets for the next year
To check whether the organisation meets the laws, rules and policies that apply to it
To find out which staff member should be disciplined
To prepare the yearly financial statements for shareholders

questions.stem: Ann-Marie Clarke is planning a compliance audit of a hotel's food safety practice. What are the "audit criteria" for this audit?
options: The names of the staff who will be interviewed
The dates and times the audit team will visit the kitchen
The list of faults found on the last visit
The rules and standards the work is checked against

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the scope of a compliance audit?
options: The areas, sites, activities and time period the audit covers
The final grade the auditor gives the department
The number of non-conformities the auditor expects to find
The penalty the firm will pay if it fails the audit

questions.stem: A distribution company in Spanish Town has time to audit only three of its ten compliance areas this year. How should the compliance manager choose them?
options: Audit the areas that were easiest to audit last year
Audit the areas whose managers ask to be audited
Audit the areas with the highest compliance risk first
Audit the areas in alphabetical order over the years

questions.stem: Before planning the year's audits, a compliance manager lists every law, licence and standard the business must meet. What is the main use of this list?
options: To decide which staff get a pay rise
To replace the need for any audits
To set criteria and choose areas to audit
To show customers how many rules the firm follows

questions.stem: Which person is best placed to audit the payroll department's compliance with the leave policy?
options: A trained auditor from outside the payroll department
The payroll supervisor, because she knows the work best
A payroll clerk chosen by the payroll supervisor
The payroll officer who processed most of the leave

questions.stem: Which item belongs in the plan for a compliance audit?
options: The disciplinary action for each likely finding
The auditee's personal performance ratings
The final audit opinion, written in advance
The objectives, scope, criteria, schedule and team

questions.stem: Why does an auditor usually agree the audit dates with the manager of the area being audited?
options: So the manager can hide any problems before the visit
So the right people and records are available on the day
So the manager can choose which records the auditor sees
So the audit can be cancelled if the area is busy

questions.stem: When might an unannounced compliance check be justified?
options: When there are signs that practice changes once a check is announced
When the auditor would prefer not to prepare an audit plan
When the manager of the area has asked for advance notice
When the company wants to catch out a staff member it dislikes

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of preparing an audit checklist from the criteria before the audit?
options: It removes the need to look at any records on the day
It lets the auditor finish in half the planned time
It makes sure each requirement is checked in the same way
It tells the auditee in advance what the findings will be

questions.stem: An auditor is following her checklist closely when she notices a fire exit blocked by boxes. Fire exits are not on the checklist. What should she do?
options: Ignore it, because fire exits are not on the checklist
Raise it with the manager at once and record it
Move the boxes herself and leave it out of the report
Note it for a future audit that includes fire safety

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the opening meeting of a compliance audit?
options: To tell the auditee what the findings are likely to be
To decide who will be blamed for any faults found
To agree the corrective actions before any checking starts
To confirm the plan, timetable and ground rules

questions.stem: Which of these is objective audit evidence?
options: A manager's opinion that staff "usually" follow the rule
The auditor's feeling that the store looks untidy
A rumour that the night shift skips the checks
Signed temperature logs for the past month

questions.stem: A warehouse supervisor tells the auditor that all forklift drivers are trained. What is the best way to confirm this?
options: Check training records for a sample of drivers
Accept it, because the supervisor is senior and should know
Ask the supervisor to put the same statement in writing
Ask one driver whether all the others have been trained

questions.stem: A firm issued 240 GCT invoices in the quarter. The auditor will check a 10% sample. How many invoices is that?
Why should an auditor choose a sample at random, or by a set method, rather than letting the auditee pick the records?
options: So the audit takes less time
So the sample is not chosen to hide problems
So the auditee does not have to find any records
So the auditor can avoid checking older records

questions.stem: Which interview approach gives an auditor the most reliable information from staff?
options: Open questions, asked calmly, then checked against records
Leading questions that suggest the answer the auditor wants
Questions asked in front of the staff member's manager to save time
Questions that threaten discipline if the answer is wrong

questions.stem: Why should an auditor watch a task being done, as well as read the written procedure for it?
options: Because written procedures are never really needed
Because watching is quicker than reading
Because staff prefer to be watched
Because practice may differ from the procedure

questions.stem: Why must an auditor keep clear working papers during the audit?
options: So the auditee can rewrite them after the audit
So the findings can be changed later if a manager complains
So each finding can be traced back to its evidence
So the audit report can be kept short

questions.stem: During a hotel audit, the auditor finds that no fire drill has been held for two years, although the hotel's own policy and its licence conditions require regular drills. How should this usually be graded?
options: An observation only
A major non-conformity
A minor non-conformity
An opportunity for improvement

questions.stem: One of 40 staff files checked is missing a signed confidentiality form; the other 39 are complete. How is this best graded?
options: A major non-conformity
A minor non-conformity
Full compliance, needing no action
A breach that must be reported to the police

questions.stem: What is an "opportunity for improvement" in a compliance audit report?
options: A suggestion where the rule is met but could be met better
A failure to meet a legal requirement in the criteria
A requirement the auditor did not have time to check
A finding that the manager of the area has refused to accept

questions.stem: An auditor checks 40 cash-up sheets. 34 are signed by two people, as the policy requires. What is the compliance rate?
Drivers at a warehouse keep missing the daily forklift pre-use check. Which approach best finds the root cause?
options: Warn the drivers that the next miss means discipline
Count how many checks were missed last year
Ask "why" several times to reach the cause
Replace the check sheet with a longer one

questions.stem: A food store's audit finds out-of-date items on a shelf. Removing them is a correction. What would be a corrective action?
options: Fixing the stock-rotation system
Throwing the out-of-date items away at once
Writing the items off as damaged stock
Selling items near their date at a lower price

questions.stem: At the closing meeting, the manager of the audited area disagrees with a finding. What should the auditor do?
options: Remove the finding to keep a good working relationship
End the meeting and report the manager for being rude
Lower the grade until the manager agrees to accept it
Review the evidence with him and note any disagreement

questions.stem: Which item belongs in a compliance audit report?
options: The auditor's personal opinions of each staff member
Findings with evidence, criteria and grading
A list of staff to be dismissed
Private notes from interviews, word for word, with names

questions.stem: Which sentence is best for a finding in an audit report?
options: Staff in the warehouse are very careless about safety at all times.
The stores area is in a bad state and the supervisor does not care.
3 of 10 extinguishers checked had no service tag dated this year.
Some things in the kitchen could be done better than they are now.

questions.stem: Who should normally receive the final compliance audit report?
options: Every staff member, the customers and the local press
Only the auditor, who files it for the next audit
The audited area's manager and the audit sponsor
The firm's competitors, so they can compare results

questions.stem: What should a corrective action plan include for each finding?
options: The action, who will do it and the date it is due
A general promise that the team will try to do better
The auditor's name, qualifications and contact details
The date of next year's audit and who will attend it

questions.stem: Three months after an audit, the manager reports that all corrective actions are complete. What should the auditor do?
options: Close all the findings on the manager's word
Start a full new audit of every area
Remove the findings from the records
Verify with evidence that each action works

questions.stem: Of 24 corrective actions due by the end of June, 6 are still open. What percentage are overdue?
A department head has ignored corrective actions from two audits in a row, and one finding is a legal breach. What should the compliance manager do?
options: Escalate it to senior management or the audit committee
Remove the finding so the department's results look better
Keep sending the head a reminder by email every month
Fix the department's problem herself and tell nobody

questions.stem: During an audit of staff files, the auditor sees medical details about an employee. What should she do?
options: Mention it to her colleagues so they can offer support
Copy the details into the audit report as evidence
Keep it private and record only what the audit needs
Tell the employee's supervisor about the condition

questions.stem: An audit of a customer database finds personal data kept long after the business needs it. Which requirement does this most likely breach?
options: The tax rules on filing GCT returns each month
The company's dress code and uniform policy
The fire safety rules for public buildings
The data protection law on keeping data

questions.stem: During an audit, a manager offers the auditor a free weekend at the company's hotel "as thanks". What should the auditor do?
options: Accept it, as long as the report is finished first
Decline it politely and report the offer
Accept it quietly and tell nobody about it
Accept it and soften the findings in return

questions.stem: Why should a compliance auditor study the relevant laws and standards before the audit?
options: To judge fairly whether practice meets them
To be able to do the auditee's job during the visit
To avoid having to read the documents on site
To find faults that are not in the criteria

questions.stem: An audit finds that a serious workplace injury last month may not have been reported as the law requires. What should the auditor do?
options: Leave it out, as the worker has already recovered
Report it straight to the media and the public
Tell the injured worker to report it himself
Raise it urgently with senior management

questions.stem: A hotel's policy requires all 60 food handlers to hold a current Food Handler's Permit. The auditor finds 54 with current permits. What percentage comply?
A compliance risk is rated 4 for likelihood and 5 for impact on a 1–5 scale. The score is likelihood × impact. What is its score?
An audit needs 3 auditors for 4 days each at J$25,000 per auditor-day. What is the cost of the auditors' time?
Which arrangement best keeps a business compliant between audits?
options: A compliance calendar with owners and self-checks
Waiting for the next inspection by the authorities
Asking every staff member to read the laws each year
Running an audit only after a complaint

questions.stem: What is the main difference between an internal and an external compliance audit?
options: Internal audits do not need any evidence at all
External audits are always cheaper and quicker
Whether the auditors work for the firm or not
Internal audits are done only once every ten years

questions.stem: A hotel group must keep its operating licence. Why should its internal audit check the licence conditions before the regulator's inspection?
options: So staff can be told what to say to the inspector
So any gaps are found and fixed first
So the inspection can be cancelled
So the regulator does not need to visit

questions.stem: How can a compliance manager best judge whether the audit programme is working?
options: Track repeat findings and actions closed on time
Count how many pages each audit report has
Ask the auditors whether they enjoyed the audits
Check that every audit found at least ten faults

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What two-word term names the set of requirements that a compliance audit measures practice against?
What term names a failure, found in an audit, to meet a requirement? (One word, often written with a hyphen.)
A store has 360 delivery notes for the month. The auditor checks 5% of them. How many notes is that?
An auditor checks 50 vehicle logbooks and finds 46 fully completed. What is the compliance rate, as a percentage?
What two-word term names the auditor's own record of the evidence gathered and the checks done during an audit?
What two-word term names the meeting at the end of an audit where the auditor presents the findings to the auditee?
What two-word term names the underlying reason a non-conformity happened, which a corrective action must remove?
Name the simple technique of asking "why?" again and again until the cause of a problem is reached. (Two words.)
On a 1–5 scale, a compliance risk scores 2 for likelihood and 5 for impact. Using likelihood × impact, what is its score?
What one word describes an auditor who has no personal interest in, or responsibility for, the area being audited?
What three-word term names the plan that sets out the actions, owners and due dates to fix the findings of an audit?
An audit takes 2 auditors 5 days each at J$28,000 per auditor-day. What is the total cost of their time, in J$?
Of 30 corrective actions due this quarter, 24 were closed on time. What percentage were closed on time?
What two-word term names the list of all the laws, licences, permits and standards a business must comply with, with an owner for each?
What two-word term names a sample in which every record has an equal chance of being chosen?

essays.stem: You are asked to carry out an internal compliance audit of a Montego Bay hotel's health and safety practice. Describe the audit plan you would prepare and explain why each part is needed.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by agreeing the objective with the general manager: to find out whether the hotel meets health and safety law, its licence conditions and its own safety policy. The scope would set the areas (kitchen, laundry, pool, maintenance and guest rooms), the shifts and the period, for example the last twelve months. The criteria would be listed from the compliance register: the safety law by its general purpose, fire safety requirements, the hotel's policies and procedures. From these I would prepare a checklist so each requirement is checked the same way. The plan would name the audit team, who must be independent of the areas, and give a timetable with an opening meeting, site visits on day and night shifts, interviews, record checks and a closing meeting. It would state the sampling method, for example 10% of maintenance job cards chosen at random. I would agree dates with the managers so records and staff are available, and set out how findings will be graded, reported and followed up. A clear plan keeps the audit fair, focused and within time.
markingPoints: States a clear objective agreed with the sponsor
Defines the scope: areas, shifts and period
Lists the criteria and turns them into a checklist
Names an independent team, timetable and sampling method
Explains how findings will be graded, reported and followed up

essays.stem: Explain how a compliance manager should build a yearly, risk-based compliance audit programme for a manufacturing company with many legal and licence obligations.
essays.modelAnswer: The manager should begin with a compliance register that lists every obligation: safety, environmental permits, product standards, tax and GCT records, employment law, data protection and licence conditions, each with an owner. Each obligation is then rated for risk, usually likelihood times impact, using evidence such as past audit findings, incidents, complaints, changes in the law, new processes and staff turnover. The areas with the highest scores are audited first and most often, perhaps twice a year, while low-risk areas may be audited every two or three years or checked by self-assessment. The programme should set out which areas are audited in which quarter, the criteria, the lead auditor and the days needed, so it can be costed and staffed. It must avoid placing auditors in their own areas. The programme should be approved by senior management or the audit committee and reviewed during the year, so that a serious incident or a new law can bring an audit forward. This approach spends limited audit time where failure would do the most harm.
markingPoints: Starts from a complete register of obligations with owners
Rates each area for risk using evidence
Sets audit frequency by risk, with low-risk areas checked less often
Schedules, costs and staffs the audits with independent auditors
Has the programme approved and reviewed when risks change

essays.stem: Compare documents, interviews and observation as sources of audit evidence, and explain how an auditor should use them together.
essays.modelAnswer: Documents and records, such as logs, permits, training records and invoices, are strong evidence because they are fixed, dated and can be sampled. Their weakness is that a record can be filled in without the work being done, or written up later. Interviews show how staff understand a requirement and can reveal problems that records hide, but people may give the answer they think the auditor wants, or describe what should happen rather than what does. Observation shows what is really done at the time, for example whether a cleaner dilutes a chemical correctly, but it covers only a short period and people may act differently when watched. Because each source has limits, the auditor should use them together. For example, she might read the procedure, ask the operator to describe the task, watch it being done and then check the record for that shift. When all three agree, the finding is reliable; when they differ, the gap itself is useful evidence. Every piece of evidence should be noted in the working papers so the finding can be traced.
markingPoints: Explains the strengths and limits of documents
Explains the strengths and limits of interviews
Explains the strengths and limits of observation
Explains cross-checking the sources against each other, with an example
Records evidence so each finding can be traced

essays.stem: An audit of 80 staff training records at a distribution firm finds 68 complete, 9 missing one refresher course, and 3 workers operating forklifts with no training record at all. Calculate the compliance rate, grade the findings and recommend what should happen next.
essays.modelAnswer: The compliance rate is 68 out of 80, which is 85%. The 9 records missing one refresher course are 11.25% of the sample, and the 3 untrained forklift operators are 3.75%. Checking: 68 + 9 + 3 = 80, and 85 + 11.25 + 3.75 = 100. I would grade the missing refresher courses as a minor non-conformity, because the workers were trained once and the gap is in keeping the training current, unless the policy treats refresher training as essential to safety. The three untrained forklift operators are a major non-conformity, because untrained operation can cause serious injury and may break safety law and the firm's own rules. I would raise this at once with the warehouse manager so that the three stop operating forklifts until they are trained and assessed. The corrective action plan should give dates for refresher courses, find the root cause, for example no system that blocks untrained staff from the forklift roster, and fix it. I would follow up the major finding within weeks and check the roster and training records again.
markingPoints: Calculates 85% correctly (and the other shares), with a check
Grades the refresher gaps as minor with a reason
Grades untrained operators as major and acts at once for safety
Requires root cause and a corrective action plan with dates
Plans early follow-up to verify the actions

essays.stem: Describe the structure and content of a good compliance audit report, and explain why each part matters.
essays.modelAnswer: A good report opens with a short summary for senior managers: the overall result, the number of major and minor findings and the most urgent action. The next section sets out the objective, scope, criteria, dates, auditors and method, including how samples were chosen, so readers know what was and was not covered. The main body lists each finding with the requirement, what was found, the evidence and the grade, written in neutral, factual language such as "3 of 10 extinguishers had no current service tag" rather than opinions. Good practice should be noted too, as this encourages staff. Each finding should be followed by the agreed corrective action, the owner and a due date, or a note that the auditee will submit a plan by a set date. Any disagreement raised at the closing meeting should be recorded fairly. The report ends with the follow-up arrangements and is sent to the area manager and the sponsor. Personal information should be left out unless it is essential. A clear structure lets managers act quickly and lets the next auditor check progress.
markingPoints: Includes an executive summary of the overall result
States objective, scope, criteria and method
Gives each finding with requirement, evidence and grade in factual language
Includes corrective actions, owners, dates and follow-up
Explains why each part matters and protects confidential information

essays.stem: Explain why independence, objectivity and confidentiality matter in compliance auditing, and describe how an auditor can protect each of them.
essays.modelAnswer: Independence matters because an auditor who works in, manages or has a personal link to an area may overlook problems or be seen to. To protect it, the audit programme should never assign auditors to their own areas, and auditors should declare any conflict of interest, such as a relative in the department, and step aside. Objectivity means that findings are based on evidence measured against the criteria, not on opinion, friendship or pressure. The auditor protects it by using a checklist, sampling fairly, recording evidence in working papers, grading by set rules and refusing gifts or favours, reporting any that are offered. Confidentiality matters because auditors see personal data, pay details, complaints and commercial information. Misuse would harm people, damage trust and could break the data protection law. The auditor should take only the information needed, store working papers securely, leave names out of the report where possible and discuss findings only with those entitled to know. Without these three qualities, managers and regulators cannot rely on the audit's results.
markingPoints: Explains independence and protects it by assignment and declaring conflicts
Explains objectivity: evidence against criteria, not opinion
Protects objectivity with checklists, fair sampling and refusing gifts
Explains confidentiality and links it to the data protection law in general terms
Describes secure handling and limited sharing of audit information

essays.stem: At the closing meeting, a department manager rejects two of your findings and says he will complain to the general manager. Explain how you would handle the meeting and what you would do afterwards.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stay calm and polite and thank him for raising his concerns. I would remind everyone that the audit measures practice against agreed criteria and is not a judgement on him personally. For each disputed finding I would show the requirement and the evidence from my working papers, such as the sample of records and what I observed, and ask what evidence he has that I may have missed. If he gives new evidence, for example a record kept in another office, I would agree to check it before the report is final and change the finding if the evidence supports this. If the evidence still shows a non-conformity, I would keep the finding but record his disagreement fairly in the report. I would not lower a grade simply to avoid conflict, because that would make the audit unreliable. I would agree the next steps: when he will receive the draft report and when his corrective action plan is due. Afterwards I would brief the audit sponsor, so that the general manager hears the facts first, and keep notes of the meeting.
markingPoints: Stays calm, respectful and focused on criteria rather than the person
Reviews the requirement and evidence for each disputed finding
Considers new evidence and changes a finding only if evidence supports it
Records unresolved disagreement rather than dropping the finding
Agrees next steps and briefs the sponsor, keeping notes

essays.stem: Explain how corrective action should be planned and followed up after a compliance audit, so that the same findings do not appear again at the next audit.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the manager of the area should make an immediate correction where there is a risk, for example removing out-of-date stock or stopping an unsafe practice. Then, for each finding, the team should look for the root cause, using a method such as the five whys or a cause-and-effect diagram, because fixing only the symptom lets the problem return. The corrective action plan should set out the action that removes the cause, such as changing a procedure, adding a system check or training staff, with a named owner, the resources needed and a realistic due date. Major findings should have shorter deadlines. The auditor or compliance manager should review the plan to make sure the actions match the causes. Progress should be tracked on a log and reported to senior management, with overdue actions escalated. At follow-up, the auditor should verify with evidence, such as new records or observation, that each action was done and is working, before closing the finding. Repeat findings should be analysed across the business to spot wider weaknesses.
markingPoints: Separates immediate correction from corrective action
Finds the root cause with a named method
Plans actions with owners, resources and dates, shorter for major findings
Tracks progress and escalates overdue actions
Verifies with evidence before closing and analyses repeat findings

essays.stem: Plan the main checks you would make in a compliance audit of how a retail chain collects, uses, stores and disposes of customers' personal data. Refer to the data protection law by its general purpose only.
essays.modelAnswer: The data protection law aims to make sure personal data is collected fairly for a clear purpose, kept accurate and secure, used only as people have been told, kept no longer than needed and disposed of safely, with people able to see their own data. My criteria would be these principles, the chain's privacy policy and its retention schedule. I would check the loyalty card form and website to see whether customers are told what data is collected and why, and whether consent is recorded where it is needed. I would sample customer records to see whether more data is collected than needed and whether it is accurate. I would check who can access the database, whether passwords and access rights match job roles and whether laptops are protected. I would observe how paper forms are stored and shredded, and check the retention schedule against the age of records held. I would ask how a request from a customer to see their data is handled, and how a data breach would be reported. Each finding would be graded and reported confidentially.
markingPoints: States the general purpose of the data protection law correctly, without sections
Checks collection: notice, purpose and consent
Checks accuracy, access controls and security
Checks retention and safe disposal against the schedule
Checks handling of access requests and breaches, and reports confidentially

essays.stem: Evaluate the use of the company's own staff compared with an outside firm for compliance audits, and recommend an approach for a medium-sized Jamaican business with 150 staff.
essays.modelAnswer: Internal auditors know the business, its systems and its people, so they can plan quickly, understand the context of a finding and follow up easily. They are cheaper per day and can audit more often. Their weaknesses are that they may lack specialist knowledge of some laws, may be too close to colleagues, and may feel pressure from senior managers, which can weaken independence. An outside firm brings specialist skills, a fresh view and clear independence, and its report may carry more weight with a board, lenders or a regulator. However, it costs more, needs time to learn the business and may give general recommendations that do not fit the firm. For a business of 150 staff, I would recommend a mixed approach. Trained internal staff, never auditing their own areas, should carry out a risk-based programme of routine audits each year. An outside firm should be used every two or three years, or for high-risk specialist areas such as data protection or safety, to give independent assurance and train the internal team. This balances cost, skill and independence.
markingPoints: Gives the strengths of internal auditors
Gives the weaknesses of internal auditors, including independence
Gives the strengths and weaknesses of an outside firm, including cost
Makes a clear recommendation suited to a 150-staff business
Justifies the recommendation by balancing cost, skill and independence

practical1.title: Plan and carry out a compliance audit of a Centre area
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a short set of criteria for one area of the Centre, such as the reception office, a computer room or the stores (for example: fire exits clear, extinguishers in date, first aid box stocked and checked, visitor sign-in kept, personal records locked away, safety signs in place, cleaning chemicals labelled and stored). As a group, plan the audit, carry it out and record the evidence. First, write a one-page audit plan with the objective, scope, criteria, timetable and sampling method. Next, turn the criteria into a checklist. Then hold a short opening meeting with the assessor, who plays the area manager. Carry out the audit by checking records, observing the area and asking one or two staff questions (the assessor arranges who may be asked). Finally, grade each finding as compliant, minor, major or an opportunity for improvement, with the evidence. Give each member a named role: lead auditor (writes the plan and runs the opening meeting), checklist officer (prepares the checklist and keeps it up to date during the audit), records checker (samples and checks records), observer and interviewer (checks the area and asks the questions), and recorder (keeps the working papers and grades the findings with the group). In a group of four, the lead auditor also acts as recorder. Photograph each stage and hand in the plan, checklist, working papers and graded findings.
materials: Audit criteria for one Centre area, from the assessor
Blank audit plan and checklist templates (optional)
Clipboards, pens and coloured sticky labels for grading
A computer and printer, or flipchart paper and markers
photos: The audit plan with objective, scope, criteria and timetable
The checklist prepared from the criteria
The opening meeting with the assessor (notes and table only if anyone prefers no face)
Members checking the area and the records (no personal details visible)
The completed working papers with evidence noted against each item
The graded findings sheet with any compliance rates worked out
checklist: Took a named role and completed their part of the evidence
Plan states a clear objective, scope, criteria and sampling method
Checklist covers every criterion in a form that can be ticked with evidence
Gathered objective evidence by records, observation or questions, not opinion
Findings are graded sensibly, with the evidence for each, and any rate is correct
Kept personal information private and did not photograph it
Spoke politely and professionally to the area manager and staff
safety: Do not open locked cabinets or read personal records unless the assessor allows it; record only what the audit needs
Do not photograph personal details, screens with private data or people who have not agreed
Report any real hazard you find, such as a blocked exit, to the assessor at once instead of fixing it yourself
Move around the area carefully, keep walkways clear and do not disturb staff at work more than needed

practical2.title: Report a compliance audit, hold the closing meeting and plan corrective action
practical2.brief: The assessor gives your group the working papers from a made-up compliance audit of a business, for example a guest house, a small factory or a distribution depot. The pack includes the criteria, sampled records with counts, observation notes, interview notes and one finding the area manager is known to dispute. As a group: (1) work out the compliance rate for each sampled item and check every figure twice; (2) grade each finding as major, minor or an opportunity for improvement, with reasons; (3) hold a 20-minute closing meeting as a role play, with one member playing the area manager who disputes a finding; (4) write a two-page audit report with a summary, scope, findings and evidence; (5) prepare a corrective action plan with root causes, actions, owners, dates and the follow-up check for each finding. Give each member a named role: lead auditor (chairs the closing meeting), analyst (works the rates, checked by another member), report writer (drafts the report), corrective action planner (drafts the plan and follow-up dates), and area manager (plays the manager in the role play and then reviews the report for fair, factual wording). In a group of four, the analyst also plays the area manager. Photograph each stage and hand in the calculations, notes of the meeting, report and plan.
materials: Made-up audit working papers pack from the assessor
Computers with word-processing and spreadsheet software, and a printer
Report and corrective action plan templates (optional)
photos: The calculation sheet with every rate shown and the second check marked
The grading of each finding, with reasons, on the flipchart or screen
The closing meeting role play in progress (notes and table only if anyone prefers no face)
The notes of the closing meeting, showing how the disputed finding was handled
The corrective action plan with root causes, owners, dates and follow-up checks
checklist: Took a named role and completed their part of the evidence
